45	
46	### Gates before the default flips
47	
48	S8 stays behind these gates:
49	
50	- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements.
51	- Output is deterministic across checker counts on a large program.
52	- A Linux CI run of the checker path is green.
53	- Memory behaviour past 600 edits in a watch session, with the recycle threshold (768 MiB `max_rss_mib`) exercised.
54	- The tsrs-against-Go parity check (`pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity`, PR 392) passes on the pinned version, and runs on every pin change.
55	
56	The determinism and memory gates are measured by `just gate-measure`; what it reads, and why the first gate's wording cannot be met as written (tsrs's `--api` has no checker-count option), is in [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md).
57	
58	## Alternatives considered
59	
60	- **Keep the checker opt-in.** Two sources of truth, and the default keeps the silent wrong answers above.
61	- **Checker for the addon only.** The CLI and agents read the same wrong types, and they can afford to wait.
62	- **Link the tsrs crates in-process now.** Unpublished crates, a toolchain change and a pre-1.0 internal API, before the process route is measured through the Rust client.
63	- **Parse with `tsrs_parser` instead of oxc.** Unpublished like every tsrs crate, and the extractor is written against oxc's AST, which already gives the syntactic facts kept here at about 2 ms per incremental update.
64	- **Keep investing in the structural resolver.** Each defect class above re-implements a checker rule and was silent until a comparison found it.

1	# 25. The resolver owns scoping; the extractor records where a declaration sits
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-06
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Which declaration a name refers to is decided in more than one place, and none of them is the resolver.
8	
9	- The extractor keys every declaration by `scoped_key` (`extractor/mod.rs`): the file, the enclosing namespaces and the bare name. A function body or block adds no part to the key. `local_depth` (`extractor/visit.rs`, field in `extractor/mod.rs`) is read by one collector, `visit_ts_interface_declaration`, to decide whether a declaration may merge with, replace or be skipped for a module-level one. `visit_ts_type_alias_declaration` and the enum collectors in `extractor/interface.rs` insert under the same key without asking, so a local one replaces a module-level one of that name.
10	- `docs/edge-cases.md` lists what this leaves open: a local interface, enum or class is not isolated from a module-level one of the same name, two local ones overwrite each other, and an interface directly in a `switch` case counts as module-level, because `visit_switch_statement` raises `block_depth` but not `local_depth`.
11	- The resolver's `TypeScope` (`types/scope.rs`, held in `ResolveState.scope` in `types/global.rs`) binds type parameters only. Its doc comment says declarations sit at module level, so the resolver has no notion of a declaration's scope to consult.
12	- `ImportRef.is_type_only` (`import_map.rs`) is copied from the import and carries `#[allow(dead_code)]`; only that file's tests read it. The one reader of `ImportBinding.is_type_only` is `promote_reexported_imports` in `extractor/mod.rs`, which folds it into a re-export, so the extractor decides a status the resolver never sees.
13	
14	Each scope fix so far was a rule added to one collector, and each collector got its own rule. The next kind of declaration or block repeats the question.
15	
16	## Decision
17	
18	The resolver owns name resolution and scoping. The extractor records every declaration and never decides which one a name refers to.
19	
20	- Every collected declaration (interface, alias, enum, class) carries its enclosing scope identity, assigned by the extractor from where the declaration sits: module, namespace, function body, block, or `switch` case. The extractor stops dropping, merging or replacing declarations by name. Two declarations that differ in scope are two entries.
21	- The resolver looks a name up from the reference's scope outward, with `TypeScope` or a sibling type beside it, so type parameters and declarations shadow under one rule. Merging of same-scope declarations (interfaces, enums) moves with it.
22	- `is_type_only` is recorded once, by the extractor, on the import. The resolver reads it from `ImportRef`; nothing re-derives it, and the `dead_code` allowance goes.
23	
24	## Consequences
25	
26	- `local_depth`, `module_interfaces` and the module-level checks in `visit_ts_interface_declaration` go away. The `docs/edge-cases.md` entries on local declarations and the `switch` case are removed when the branch that closes them lands.
27	- Collected shapes gain a scope identity, which changes `SourceData`. That is a positional MessagePack change (ADR 0003): `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`cache.rs`) moves with it and `cache/golden.rs` fails until it does. A change to the canonical JSON would follow ADR 0017.
28	- Lookup by scope costs a walk outward per reference where it is a map hit today, and entries per name grow. Each resolver branch needs the Chakra plus dependencies run for peak RSS and wall time against `main`, with the addon's real configuration (collapse `none`), not only a fixture.
29	- Follow-up branches, each small and independent of the later ones, in this order:
30	  1. Add the scope identity to collected declarations and populate it, with no reader. Bumps `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
31	  2. Resolve interfaces by scope; drop `local_depth` and `module_interfaces`. Closes the interface half of the edge case.
32	  3. Give a `switch` case its own scope in the walk, so a declaration directly in a case is local.
33	  4. Do the same for aliases and enums, then classes.
34	  5. Read `ImportRef.is_type_only` in the resolver where type-only status matters, and remove the `dead_code` allowance. If nothing there needs it, remove the field instead.
35	- Unsolved: declaration merging across scopes that TypeScript allows (a `namespace` merging with an interface or class), global and ambient augmentation, and `typeof` and value-space shadowing are out of this decision. The structural pass stays an approximation, and the opt-in backend of ADR 0006 is still the answer where it must match the compiler.
36	- Risk: until branch 2 lands the extractor and resolver disagree about scope. Branch 1 reads nothing, so it changes no output; the later branches change output only where the edge case applied.
37	
38	## Alternatives considered
39	
40	- Keep patching in the extractor, as `local_depth` did for interfaces. Each collector still decides alone, the aliases, enums and classes need a copy of the rule, and a reference is resolved in the resolver on a key the extractor has already collapsed. The information a scope-aware lookup needs is gone by then.
41	- Move all scoping into the extractor, resolving each reference to a unique key while it walks. The extractor would then answer which declaration a name means, but it sees one file; imports, re-exports, dependency declarations and type arguments are only known to the resolver, so it would have to resolve twice or leave the cross-file half unscoped.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/skills/rust-style

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.

**Goal:** Every public type is immediately usable, visible in error messages, and extendable without semver breaks.

## Checklist before merging a new `pub struct` or `pub enum`

- `#[derive(Debug)]` — always
- `impl Display` — if it appears in messages, CLI output, or diagnostic text
- `impl std::error::Error` — if it represents a failure condition
- `impl AsRef<str>` — on string newtypes
- `#[non_exhaustive]` — on enums that will gain variants; adding one without this is a semver break
- `#[must_use]` — on functions whose return value the caller must not silently drop

## Wire or don't define

A new abstraction needs a real call site in the same PR — not a follow-up ticket. An unused type adds noise and false confidence. If the use case isn't clear yet, leave a note in the doc instead.

Reference: `crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs` — canonical complete type in this project.

A trail captures project intent across repositories and branches. Manage intent and discussions on the whole trail; use --repo and --branch to select context for checkout, sessions, findings, and approvals.

Usage:
  entire trail [flags]
  entire trail [command]

Available Commands:
  approvals       List approval decisions on a trail
  approve         Approve a trail
  checkout        Check out a trail's branch
  comment         Discuss the whole trail across repositories
  create          Create a trail and publish its branch
  finding         Manage a trail's agent findings
  link            Link a repository branch to a trail
  list            List trails in a project
  merge           Merge one of a trail's changes into its base
  resume          Resume a trail's agent session
  show            Show trail intent and its repositories and branches
  unlink          Unlink a repository branch without deleting its work
  update          Update project intent and lifecycle
  watch           Tail events for a trail's selected repository branch

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for trail
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace

=== PR 399: perf(semantic): memoize the converter by what a conversion asked of its context [perf/converter-memo] MERGED
BODY: Fixes the converter memo cost disclosed on #394: recursion identity became the type handle (the instantiation), which made the memo key far finer than before. Only `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` plus new tests and fixtures change; output is unchanged.

The key and why it is sound (the argument is in a comment next to `State::memo`):
- The memo is keyed by (type handle, depth). Each key holds a list of entries; an entry records the set of handles its conversion compared against the enclosing instantiations (`asked`), each found or absent, plus the subset that did enclose it (`enclosed_by`).
- An entry is reused in a context only when the enclosing set matches it on every handle in `asked` (`Entry::holds_in`).
- A conversion reads its context only through depth (which is in the key) and `Cx::encloses`, so it is a deterministic walk fixed by the type, the depth and the answers to those questions. With the same answers it asks the same questions in the same order and returns the same result. Entries that hold in a context all agree, so discovery order cannot show in the output.
- Handles the conversion opened itself are dropped from the recorded set, because each was recorded absent at its own gate.
- Absent answers must be recorded, not only back-reference hits; the worker confirmed this by mutation: recording only hits fails the new soundness test.

Tests (`crates/semantic/tests/memo.rs`, fixtures `memo` and `cycles` with recordings; each runs replayed and live, forward and reversed):
- `a_type_many_types_enclose_is_converted_once` (16 interfaces and 12 union-member aliases sharing one big type, plus nested `Box<T>`): on main it fails with 1,211 round trips against a bound of 300; with the fix it takes 274.
- `a_type_inside_and_outside_a_cycle_is_a_back_reference_only_inside`: main is already sound, so this is a guard, not a fix test; it does fail the hit-only mutation above.

Measured with the Rust client and tsrs 0.23.0, 9 interleaved runs, medians, load average 5.5 to 6.4 at the start of runs:
- Big project (1,138-prop `ButtonProps`): round trips 6,970 to 4,874 (the pre-regression value), memo hits and misses 945 and 42,837 to 35,309 and 6,241, time 628 to 546 ms, peak RSS 128.6 to 128.9 MB.
- The `chakra` project (8 components, `/tmp/claude-501/spike/proj/chakra`, not `fixtures/chakra`): round trips about 8,060 to about 8,066, time 767.6 to 765.2 ms. On this project the round trips vary from 8,060 to 8,079 between runs because concurrent tasks race on the memo.

Byte identity: the per-prop dump is identical to main on the big project and on `chakra` (`cmp`); the 14-case snapshot test, the `Loop` and mutual-recursion tests, `every_cap_cuts_where_it_is_set` and the reverse-order test pass. The checker lane gives identical verdicts and types on all 212 rows (176 identical, 27 spelled, 1 wrong, 6 less precise, 2 opaque with marker); parity is 212 identical.

Gates in a clean-room worktree: `just lint doc-check machete typos` and `just semver` exit 0; `cargo check` (clippy, workspace, all targets) exit 0; nextest with `TSRS_BIN` set 1,367 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. No changeset, since nothing is user-visible. Not verified: memory beyond the RSS above.

=== PR 400: feat(semantic): keep React DOM attribute families, own members and base layers (ADR 0026 S3) [feat/react-families] MERGED
BODY: Slice S3 of ADR 0026: React's DOM attribute types are kept as a family instead of being expanded into hundreds of fields, and a project interface keeps its own members while inherited dependency members are no longer inlined. Stacked on #399 (`perf/converter-memo`); merge that first. If #399 merges and its branch is deleted, retarget this PR to main before merging. Only `crates/semantic` changes.

What it does:
- Family recognition by identity and declaring path: a type is a React DOM family if it is declared in `/@types/react/` and is `HTMLAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLProps`, `AllHTMLAttributes`, `SVGAttributes`, `SVGProps`, an element-specific `*HTMLAttributes`, or `DetailedHTMLProps` (followed through its first alias argument). It becomes `HtmlAttributes { element, omitted: [] }`, with the element from the interface name or from its type argument (`HTMLAnchorElement` gives `a`) through core's existing `html_element_for` and `html_element_from_type_arg`. An unknown element is not guessed. A family outside a wrapper stays the `named` it was, so existing output does not change.
- Wrappers: `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required` and `Readonly` stay as `Named{name, [first argument, key args]}` when the type is over budget and the first argument is a family or a dependency or lib type; under budget they expand (`Pick<ComponentProps<"button">, "disabled" | "type">`, 2 props, is expanded). The checker does not keep `ComponentPropsWithoutRef`, so `react/13` comes out as `Omit<Omit<html:a,"ref">,"href">`, which is how the checker prints it. `Record` is not a wrapper, since its first argument is the key type.
- Own versus inherited: a property is the project's own if its first declaration is in a file that is neither under `node_modules` nor a lib file. The converter calls `getBaseTypes {type}` (new `base_types` in `rpc.rs`), only when the type is over budget. An over-budget class or interface becomes an intersection of its own fields and its base layers; a base declared in the project is followed to its own bases. An instantiation of a generic interface states no bases (the API returns null), so its outside members come out as `Truncated` with their real count beside its own fields.
- Budget: the 100 and 40 field limits now count only members that are not the project's own, or that have no declaration. They produce `Truncated { Members { total } }` with the real count and never touch own fields. Depth is unchanged. Union and intersection member caps are unchanged, so the 600 and 501 member rows in the cases fixture are still cut, and over-budget types with call signatures are still truncated whole.
- Terminals: a union holding `ReactElement`, `ReactPortal`, an `Iterable` of `ReactNode` (found by its argument's alias) and the primitives becomes `ReactNode` plus the remaining members, so `react/07` is now `[reactNode, function]`. `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element` stay collapsed, as decided in ADR 0026.

A heuristic to review: `as?: ElementType` inside `BoxProps` (`react/34`) was cut at the nested union limit (181 members). A union wider than the budget that holds more than 100 string literals plus `ComponentClass` and `FunctionComponent` is now kept as `elementType`. This is a threshold-based rule, it only fires over budget, and top-level and constrained uses are unchanged.

What the checker lane shows, stated plainly (212 rows, all diffed before and after): identical 176, spelled 27 to 28, wrong 1, less precise 6 to 7, opaque with marker 2 to 0. `react/13` goes from opaque with marker to spelled (a real improvement). `react/34` goes from opaque with marker to less precise: it is no longer truncated and has no `degradedBy`, but the golden is a 279-field object so identical was not reachable, and the lane's rank order counts that as worse. `react/07` is still less precise against its golden, but its type is now the union above with no 20-member expansion. `generics/10`, `11` and `12` are still identical, with their type changed from a truncated `Omit` to a named wrapper. So of the three rows I expected to turn green, only `react/13` is clearer; the others are better in substance and not green. On `objects/23-symbol-keyed` (out of scope): `[tag]` is correct and the golden's internal name `__@tag@id` is the artifact.

Byte difference against #399: the big project and the chakra project are identical apart from `stats.durationMs`. `rdt-compat`, added as a check, has exactly one difference: `TypeSampler.buttonProps` goes from `Truncated Omit{275}` to `Named Omit<html:button,…>`. Timing (9 interleaved runs, medians, load average about 6.9 and 6.5, read from the semantic backend's debug line): big 4,874 against 4,874 round trips and 503 against 501 ms; chakra 8,050 against 8,049 and 313 against 312 ms.

Tests: the new `crates/semantic/tests/families.rs` (fixture `families`: own 150-field interface, dependency 150-field interface, `Pick`, `Omit` over `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `DetailedHTMLProps`, `BoxProps`, a `ReactNode` union, a wide `ElementType`) fails on the old source (9 failed) and passes after; recorded from real tsrs, it replays always and runs live, forward and reversed, when `TSRS_BIN` is set. The `cases` snapshot and recording are re-recorded and its `wideTop` and `wide` assertions now expect uncut own interfaces. One patch changeset and the converter section of `docs/type-checker-integration.md`.

BODY: ## What

ADR 0026 S6. In watch mode an edit is applied to the kept checker snapshot with `updateSnapshot`, instead of building a new program for every edit, and an edit the checker was not told about now fails loudly instead of being served from old text.

Stacked on #410 (S5). Merge #410 first; GitHub retargets this PR to main when its branch is deleted.

## How

- On the pinned tsrs 0.23 and the Go 7.1 beta, `updateSnapshot` takes effect only with `ensurePrograms: true`, and an edit nobody announced is still missed. So the kept snapshot is updated with exactly the files the session announced: `WatchSession` now sends every change it applies (new `SemanticProvider::changed`).
- Before each answer, every file the checker's program read (1,855 for Chakra) has its modification time and size compared with what it had when read, about 1.5 ms. An unannounced change makes that answer come from a fresh snapshot, with a warning naming the file. Files modified within 2 s of a read are re-read every time. Content hashing cost too much on this program.
- The 64-program and RSS recycling are unchanged; a replaced process takes its snapshot with it. No serialized shape or schema change.

- Loud failure: passes. `an_edit_the_checker_is_not_told_about_fails_loudly_and_is_answered_from_the_disk` runs on tsrs and the Go checker and fails when the check is disabled.

=== PR 399: perf(semantic): memoize the converter by what a conversion asked of its context [perf/converter-memo] MERGED
BODY: Fixes the converter memo cost disclosed on #394: recursion identity became the type handle (the instantiation), which made the memo key far finer than before. Only `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` plus new tests and fixtures change; output is unchanged.

The key and why it is sound (the argument is in a comment next to `State::memo`):
- The memo is keyed by (type handle, depth). Each key holds a list of entries; an entry records the set of handles its conversion compared against the enclosing instantiations (`asked`), each found or absent, plus the subset that did enclose it (`enclosed_by`).
- An entry is reused in a context only when the enclosing set matches it on every handle in `asked` (`Entry::holds_in`).
- A conversion reads its context only through depth (which is in the key) and `Cx::encloses`, so it is a deterministic walk fixed by the type, the depth and the answers to those questions. With the same answers it asks the same questions in the same order and returns the same result. Entries that hold in a context all agree, so discovery order cannot show in the output.
- Handles the conversion opened itself are dropped from the recorded set, because each was recorded absent at its own gate.
- Absent answers must be recorded, not only back-reference hits; the worker confirmed this by mutation: recording only hits fails the new soundness test.

Tests (`crates/semantic/tests/memo.rs`, fixtures `memo` and `cycles` with recordings; each runs replayed and live, forward and reversed):
- `a_type_many_types_enclose_is_converted_once` (16 interfaces and 12 union-member aliases sharing one big type, plus nested `Box<T>`): on main it fails with 1,211 round trips against a bound of 300; with the fix it takes 274.
- `a_type_inside_and_outside_a_cycle_is_a_back_reference_only_inside`: main is already sound, so this is a guard, not a fix test; it does fail the hit-only mutation above.

Measured with the Rust client and tsrs 0.23.0, 9 interleaved runs, medians, load average 5.5 to 6.4 at the start of runs:
- Big project (1,138-prop `ButtonProps`): round trips 6,970 to 4,874 (the pre-regression value), memo hits and misses 945 and 42,837 to 35,309 and 6,241, time 628 to 546 ms, peak RSS 128.6 to 128.9 MB.

=== PR 400: feat(semantic): keep React DOM attribute families, own members and base layers (ADR 0026 S3) [feat/react-families] MERGED
BODY: Slice S3 of ADR 0026: React's DOM attribute types are kept as a family instead of being expanded into hundreds of fields, and a project interface keeps its own members while inherited dependency members are no longer inlined. Stacked on #399 (`perf/converter-memo`); merge that first. If #399 merges and its branch is deleted, retarget this PR to main before merging. Only `crates/semantic` changes.

What it does:
- Family recognition by identity and declaring path: a type is a React DOM family if it is declared in `/@types/react/` and is `HTMLAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLProps`, `AllHTMLAttributes`, `SVGAttributes`, `SVGProps`, an element-specific `*HTMLAttributes`, or `DetailedHTMLProps` (followed through its first alias argument). It becomes `HtmlAttributes { element, omitted: [] }`, with the element from the interface name or from its type argument (`HTMLAnchorElement` gives `a`) through core's existing `html_element_for` and `html_element_from_type_arg`. An unknown element is not guessed. A family outside a wrapper stays the `named` it was, so existing output does not change.
- Wrappers: `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required` and `Readonly` stay as `Named{name, [first argument, key args]}` when the type is over budget and the first argument is a family or a dependency or lib type; under budget they expand (`Pick<ComponentProps<"button">, "disabled" | "type">`, 2 props, is expanded). The checker does not keep `ComponentPropsWithoutRef`, so `react/13` comes out as `Omit<Omit<html:a,"ref">,"href">`, which is how the checker prints it. `Record` is not a wrapper, since its first argument is the key type.
- Own versus inherited: a property is the project's own if its first declaration is in a file that is neither under `node_modules` nor a lib file. The converter calls `getBaseTypes {type}` (new `base_types` in `rpc.rs`), only when the type is over budget. An over-budget class or interface becomes an intersection of its own fields and its base layers; a base declared in the project is followed to its own bases. An instantiation of a generic interface states no bases (the API returns null), so its outside members come out as `Truncated` with their real count beside its own fields.
- Budget: the 100 and 40 field limits now count only members that are not the project's own, or that have no declaration. They produce `Truncated { Members { total } }` with the real count and never touch own fields. Depth is unchanged. Union and intersection member caps are unchanged, so the 600 and 501 member rows in the cases fixture are still cut, and over-budget types with call signatures are still truncated whole.
- Terminals: a union holding `ReactElement`, `ReactPortal`, an `Iterable` of `ReactNode` (found by its argument's alias) and the primitives becomes `ReactNode` plus the remaining members, so `react/07` is now `[reactNode, function]`. `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element` stay collapsed, as decided in ADR 0026.

A heuristic to review: `as?: ElementType` inside `BoxProps` (`react/34`) was cut at the nested union limit (181 members). A union wider than the budget that holds more than 100 string literals plus `ComponentClass` and `FunctionComponent` is now kept as `elementType`. This is a threshold-based rule, it only fires over budget, and top-level and constrained uses are unchanged.

What the checker lane shows, stated plainly (212 rows, all diffed before and after): identical 176, spelled 27 to 28, wrong 1, less precise 6 to 7, opaque with marker 2 to 0. `react/13` goes from opaque with marker to spelled (a real improvement). `react/34` goes from opaque with marker to less precise: it is no longer truncated and has no `degradedBy`, but the golden is a 279-field object so identical was not reachable, and the lane's rank order counts that as worse. `react/07` is still less precise against its golden, but its type is now the union above with no 20-member expansion. `generics/10`, `11` and `12` are still identical, with their type changed from a truncated `Omit` to a named wrapper. So of the three rows I expected to turn green, only `react/13` is clearer; the others are better in substance and not green. On `objects/23-symbol-keyed` (out of scope): `[tag]` is correct and the golden's internal name `__@tag@id` is the artifact.

Byte difference against #399: the big project and the chakra project are identical apart from `stats.durationMs`. `rdt-compat`, added as a check, has exactly one difference: `TypeSampler.buttonProps` goes from `Truncated Omit{275}` to `Named Omit<html:button,…>`. BODY: ## What

ADR 0026 S6. In watch mode an edit is applied to the kept checker snapshot with `updateSnapshot`, instead of building a new program for every edit, and an edit the checker was not told about now fails loudly instead of being served from old text.

Stacked on #410 (S5). Merge #410 first; GitHub retargets this PR to main when its branch is deleted.

## How

- On the pinned tsrs 0.23 and the Go 7.1 beta, `updateSnapshot` takes effect only with `ensurePrograms: true`, and an edit nobody announced is still missed. So the kept snapshot is updated with exactly the files the session announced: `WatchSession` now sends every change it applies (new `SemanticProvider::changed`).
- Before each answer, every file the checker's program read (1,855 for Chakra) has its modification time and size compared with what it had when read, about 1.5 ms. An unannounced change makes that answer come from a fresh snapshot, with a warning naming the file. Files modified within 2 s of a read are re-read every time. Content hashing cost too much on this program.
- The 64-program and RSS recycling are unchanged; a replaced process takes its snapshot with it. No serialized shape or schema change.

## Gate (ADR 0026 S6)

- Loud failure: passes. `an_edit_the_checker_is_not_told_about_fails_loudly_and_is_answered_from_the_disk` runs on tsrs and the Go checker and fails when the check is disabled.
- 300 edits under the memory threshold: passes. Peak 321 to 357 MiB against 440 to 455 on the base and the 768 MiB bound; the 650-edit run peaked at 341 MiB with all answers from the checker and none stale.
- Edit-and-query p95 of at most 25 ms: passes only for a component with few props of its own in a Chakra-sized program (22.6 ms). It fails for a component built on Chakra's `ButtonProps` (p95 565 ms at best). Caliper converting its 1,140 props takes 330 to 375 ms even on an unchanged snapshot, so no sound design here closes that. The checker's CPU per edit did drop from 437 to 737 ms down to 56 to 80 ms. The wall-clock tails tracked machine load (load 10 to 29) more than the change.
- Byte identity: the edited component plus 10 others after 300 edits match a fresh session asked in reverse order (20,282,789 bytes, the same as base). Determinism: nine identical outputs. First answer is unchanged at 435 ms.
- Recommended budget: keep 25 ms for the checker's part only (the new `--props own` mode of the harness; base 83 ms) and give the `ButtonProps` form the first-answer budget, since its cost is the same conversion. This needs your decision, together with the first-answer budget.

## Checks

Local, exit codes: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just semver`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, nextest (1413 passed), `just test-checker-lane` (now runs the watch tests), `just test-construct`, and a clean-room run. `just gate-measure` exits 1 because first answer and watch p95 fail as stated; memory and determinism pass; the recipe now runs all four gates and fails at the end.

Not caught by the stale check: a file created unannounced where an import failed to resolve, and a tsconfig options change (still needs a new process). Not run: Linux, the oracle, a real Storybook session, napi and TS tests (no TS or napi code changed).

#!/bin/zsh
# Fetch findings for every trail change in the project (two pages of trails).
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pattern-audit
mkdir -p all
entire trail list --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper > all/list1.txt 2>&1
tok=$(grep -o 'page-token [^ ]*' all/list1.txt | awk '{print $2}')
entire trail list --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --page-token "$tok" > all/list2.txt 2>&1
awk '$1=="gh/orin-dx"{print $2}' all/list1.txt all/list2.txt | sort -un > all/trails.txt
while read t; do
  entire trail show $t --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper > all/show$t.txt 2>&1
done < all/trails.txt
grep -ho 'caliper/[0-9]*' all/show*.txt | sort -u > all/changes.txt
while read c; do
  n=${c#caliper/}
  [ -f f$n.json ] && cp f$n.json all/f$n.json && continue
  entire trail finding list $c --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --status any --freshness any --include-dismissed --json -n 200 > all/f$n.json 2>&1
done < all/changes.txt
wc -l all/trails.txt all/changes.txt
